Transport a trial's effect to a target population

Source: R/trnsp.R
trnsp.Rd

The average treatment effect of a randomised trial carried over to a target population whose covariates differ from the trial's, by the outcome model and by inverse odds weighting (Dahabreh et al. 2020; Westreich et al. 2017). The data hold the trial's units (s = 1), with outcome and treatment, and a sample of the target (s = 0), with the covariates only; y and d are not read outside the trial and may be NA there.

Usage

trnsp(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  s,
  x,
  target = c("transport", "generalize"),
  trim = 0,
  nboot = 200,
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'trnsp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit of the trial or the target.

y

The name of the outcome column (numbers; read in the trial).

d

The name of the treatment column: 0 or 1 in the trial, both present.

s

The name of the column marking the trial's units: 1 in the trial, 0 outside it (or TRUE, FALSE), both present.

x

The names of the covariate columns (numbers), complete in every row; for print(), an object of class trnsp.

target

"transport" or "generalize".

trim

The bound of the sampling scores, from 0 to below 0.5.

nboot

The bootstrap draws: a whole number from 0 (no standard errors) to 100000.

level

The level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647; not used without draws.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class trnsp, a list: tab, a data frame with rows om and iow (method, est, se, lo, hi); ps and w, the sampling scores and weights of every row; draws (a matrix, NA for a draw left out); nfail; and target, nboot, level, seed.

Details

The target is the rows outside the trial (target = "transport") or all rows, trial included ("generalize"). The outcome model fits the outcome on an intercept and x by least squares in each arm of the trial and averages the difference of the two predictions over the target (om). Inverse odds weighting gives each trial unit the weight of gensw() ((1 - ps) / ps to transport, 1 / ps to generalise, the sampling score ps trimmed to [trim, 1 - trim]) and takes the difference of the arms' weighted means, the weights normalised within each arm (iow; Tipton and Hartman 2023, eq. 3.10). The first is right when the outcome model is, the second when the sampling model is. Standard errors come from nboot bootstrap draws of the rows within the trial and within the rest, a draw whose fit fails left out (nfail), with normal intervals at level.

References

Dahabreh, I. J., Robertson, S. E., Steingrimsson, J. A., Stuart, E. A. and Hernan, M. A. (2020). Extending inferences from a randomized trial to a new target population. Statistics in Medicine, 39(14), 1999-2014. doi:10.1002/sim.8426

Westreich, D., Edwards, J. K., Lesko, C. R., Stuart, E. and Cole, S. R. (2017). Transportability of trial results using inverse odds of sampling weights. American Journal of Epidemiology, 186(8), 1010-1014. doi:10.1093/aje/kwx164

Tipton, E. and Hartman, E. (2023). Generalizability and transportability. In Zubizarreta, J. R., Stuart, E. A., Small, D. S. and Rosenbaum, P. R. (eds), Handbook of Matching and Weighting Adjustments for Causal Inference, ch. 3. Chapman and Hall/CRC. doi:10.1201/9781003102670

Examples

set.seed(9)
n <- 600
d <- data.frame(age = rnorm(n, 35, 10))
d$s <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.05 * (d$age - 35)))
d$t <- ifelse(d$s == 1, rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), NA)
d$y <- ifelse(d$s == 1, 0.5 * d$t + 0.02 * d$t * d$age + rnorm(n), NA)
trnsp(d, "y", "t", "s", "age", nboot = 100, seed = 1)
#> trnsp: the trial's effect transported to the rows outside it, 100 bootstrap draws (0 failed)
#>  method   est     se     lo    hi
#>      om 1.182 0.1282 0.9308 1.433
#>     iow 1.197 0.1288 0.9442 1.449
